title_waiting: Your case is with the office
titleLetterOpen: The office wants something from you
saveFailed: Could not save. Check your connection and try again.
offline: You are offline. Nothing was saved.
errFutureDate: That date is in the future. Choose the day it happened.
notAdvice: Dossierly organises your case and explains letters. It is not a lawyer and does not give legal advice.
extrasNote: Next: connect your mail and phone alerts, so Dossierly sees letters the day they arrive. Both are optional.
sitSub: Five short answers and Dossierly builds your case path.
sitRenew: My permit is ending and I need a new one
sitFamily: A permit for my spouse or child
sitFamilySub: Family members of someone working here
sitLetter: I got a letter about my case
sitLetterSub: Photograph it or forward the email
sitFirstSub: You are here on a visa now
groundTitleFamily: What is your own permit for?
groundSub: This decides the documents and the fee.
groundFamilySub: Spouse or child of a permit holder
orgEmployerPh: e.g. Northwind Data Sp. z o.o.
datesSub: Your region decides the office. Your end date decides the deadline.
stayUntil: Your current card is valid until
stayUntilFamily: The earliest card or visa end date in your family
stayUntilHint: The date printed on your card or visa. Your application must be in before it.
stayUntilLetterHint: If you have already filed, you can skip this. The letter has its own deadline.
datesNeedEnd: Choose the end date to see your deadline.
fileByBody: The last day of your legal stay (art. 105). One day late and the application can be refused.
startByHint: Start preparing on {date}: the employer step alone can take weeks.
fileByPassed: If you are still in Poland, talk to a person before you file. Free legal aid is on the letter screen.
familySub: Employers often pay for your permit only. Each family member has their own case, linked to yours.
familyEmpty: No one added. If it is just you, continue.
familyNeedOne: Add at least one family member to make their case.
birthYearError: Enter the child's year of birth.
famCheckWork: On a single permit your family can apply once you have held permits for 2 years in a row, the latest for at least 1 year (art. 159). Income needed: 823 zł net a month per person, {total} for {n}.
famCheckBlue: With an EU Blue Card your family can apply now (art. 159). Income needed: 823 zł net a month per person, {total} for {n}.
famCheckOther: Check that your own permit lets your family join you (art. 159) before they file. Income needed: 823 zł net a month per person, {total} for {n}.
planSubOne: Dossierly watches your mail and tells you what to do next, one step at a time.
planSubMany: {n} linked cases. Dossierly watches your mail and tells you what to do next, one step at a time.
planFeesTotal: Fees for everyone: {total}, paid as {n} separate transfers.
planNextEdeliveryBody: The office sends its letters there. It takes ten minutes with Profil Zaufany.
planNextLetterBody: Photograph it or forward the email. Dossierly explains it and counts the deadline.
check_peselSub: On your current card, if you have one. Not required to file.
check_trustedSub: Needed to sign in to MOS and sign the application
check_edeliverySub: The office sends letters here. Open it before you file.
check_photoSub: Taken in the last 6 months, plain light background
check_passport: Every passport page, scanned as one PDF
check_passportSub: Blank pages too. A missing page is a formal defect.
check_insurance: Health insurance for the whole stay
check_insuranceSub: ZUS confirmation from your employer, or a private policy
check_housingSub: Lease agreement, or a statement from the owner
check_annexSub: You type HR's email in MOS; MOS sends them a link that works for 30 days. MOS will not let you send without it.
check_qualificationsSub: Diploma, with a sworn Polish translation if it is not in Polish
check_universitySub: Zaświadczenie that you are studying, for this academic year
check_meansSub: Bank statement or a sponsor's declaration
check_sponsorCard: A copy of your family member's residence card
check_incomeSub: 823 zł net a month per person in the family: PIT, ZUS certificate or contract
check_civilSub: Shows how you are related. Recently issued is best.
check_translationsSub: For every document not in Polish
check_famCivil: Marriage and birth certificates for your family
check_famCivilSub: One per family member: they show the relationship
check_famTranslate: Sworn Polish translations of those certificates
check_famIncomeSub: 823 zł net a month per person (art. 159). Your income can cover the whole family.
check_feeStampSub: To the city office in {seat}, not the voivode. Your full name in the transfer title.
check_feeStampForSub: A separate transfer with {name}'s full name in the title, to the city office in {seat}
check_feeCardSub: To {office}. A different account from the stamp duty.
check_feeCardForSub: A separate transfer with {name}'s full name in the title, to {office}
feeAccountElsewhere: The account number is on your voivodeship office's website, under fees (opłaty).
feesNote: Pay before you file and attach each receipt in MOS: you cannot pay inside MOS. One transfer per person; swapping the two accounts is the most common mistake.
fileByPassedShort: Your file-by date has passed. Talk to a person before you file.
noEndDate: Add your card's end date to see your deadline.
prepareNote: Dossierly ticks documents as they arrive in your case. It never signs or sends anything for you.
fileLead: Since 27 April 2026 applications go only through MOS, online. You file it yourself; Dossierly walks you through every screen.
neverSigns: Dossierly never signs in to MOS
mos1: Sign in to MOS with Profil Zaufany
mos2: Copy the answers from your field sheet
mos2Sub: Every field prefilled from your case, in Polish
mos3Sub: Photo, passport PDF, insurance, housing, the rest of your checklist, both fee receipts
mos4Sub: MOS shows it once HR signs
mos5Sub: Only you can do this. A sent application cannot be edited.
mos6Sub: MOS does not email it to you
upoLead: MOS does not email a confirmation. Download the UPO after sending and add it here: without it, the application does not count as filed.
typeItIn: No photo? Type the date in
filedOnNeeded: Choose the date on your UPO.
filedSaved: Filing saved. Your waiting time starts.
filedOnSub: Filed {date}. This is your proof of filing on time.
noCaseNumberYetSub: The office emails it after registering your file. Dossierly saves it when it arrives.
mosDown: If MOS is down on your last day, file within 3 working days after it works again: the filing then counts from the first day of the outage (art. 225c).
waitingSub: Nothing for you to do now. Dossierly reads every letter and email the day it arrives.
noFilingDateBody: Add the date on your UPO receipt and Dossierly counts your wait.
canStaySub: Filed on time, your stay is legal until the final decision. Your certificate of legal stay (zaświadczenie) from MOS shows it.
noTravelSub: The certificate is not a travel document. Your old card stops working for travel on its end date.
noTravelSubDate: The certificate is not a travel document. Your card's travel use ends on {date}.
jobChange: Changing or losing your job? Tell us first
jobChangeSub: A new employer means a change application. Losing your job must be reported within 15 working days (art. 121).
purposeEndsSub: If the reason for your permit ends, tell the office within 15 working days (art. 113).
moveDuringSub: Send the new address to the office with your case number. Letters to the old address still count as delivered.
waitNote: {region} took {n} days on average in 2026 (MSWiA, July 2026). A long wait is normal and does not mean something is wrong.
clockSuspended: The 60-day decision period (art. 112a) does not run until after 4 March 2027 (art. 100d, Dz.U. 2026 poz. 203), so a long wait is not a delay by the office in law.
kindFormalBody: Something is missing or wrong in the application itself. At least 7 days to fix it (KPA art. 64 §2); if not fixed in time, the application is left without consideration.
kindEvidenceBody: The office asks for evidence. At least 14 days from delivery (art. 106f). Send what it asks for before the last day.
kindAppearBody: Fingerprints, passport and signature. At least 7 days' notice (art. 106e). If you do not come, the case is discontinued (art. 106i).
asksNone: Dossierly did not find a list of documents in this letter. Open it on the page to check.
didReadSub: The Polish text is kept beside the explanation
didCountSub: Each step of the count is shown below
youGatherSub: Tick each item above when you have it
youSendSub: With your case number and full name in the title
neverSends: Dossierly never sends anything for you
moreTime: If you cannot get a document in time, tell the office before the last day and ask for more time.
talkToPerson: Talk to a person about this
noLetterBody: When the office writes, show the letter to Dossierly: photograph it or forward the email. It explains it, finds the deadline and counts it.
helpLead: Dossierly is not a lawyer. For anything you are unsure about, these can help:
helpNote: Free help has limited places: write early and send your case number and the letter.
help_sip: Free legal aid for foreigners, Warsaw and online
help_npp: Free legal advice points across Poland, run with the Ministry of Justice
help_lawyer: Find a licensed legal adviser (radca prawny). Dossierly is not a law firm.
noVisitBody: The office sends a summons with the date, at least 7 days ahead (art. 106e). When it arrives, show it to Dossierly and the visit appears here.
dontMissBody: If you do not come, the office closes your case (art. 106i). If you cannot make it, ask the office for a new date before the day.
bringPassportSub: The original. They check it against your application.
warsawCounter: In Warsaw the counter takes only fingerprints and your signature. Documents go by e-Doręczenia, not on paper.
rehearseSub: Practise the questions the official may ask, in Polish
visitPlanSub: Where to go, when to leave, what to bring
phoneFlatSub: The official reads Polish, you read your language, both hear it spoken
wrapUpSub: What was asked, what you said, what to do next
counterFoot: Polish on their side, your language on yours
decisionLead: The decision comes by post or e-Doręczenia, not through MOS. Tell Dossierly what it says.
decisionNote: Dossierly organises your documents and dates. It does not write appeals or legal arguments.
deliveredNeeded: Choose the day the decision was delivered.
refusedSub: You can appeal. The last day is {date}: {n} days left.
refusedPassed: The 14 days to appeal ended on {date}. Talk to a person today about what is still possible.
personToday: Get a person to look at this today
personTodayBody: An appeal goes to the Head of the Office for Foreigners through the voivode, within 14 days of delivery (KPA art. 129 §2). Dossierly gathers your documents and dates; a lawyer or legal aid writes the appeal.
approvedUntil: Your permit is granted until {date}. The card is being printed.
approvedSub: Your permit is granted. The card is being printed.
collectWhenSub: By SMS or e-Doręczenia, usually 3–4 weeks after the decision
cardFeeDue: Card fee: check it is paid
cardFeeSub: Printing starts after the office has the card fee receipt
renewSub: Start preparing your next application on {date}. Dossierly will remind you.
renewNoDate: Add your new card's end date to get your renewal date.
loseJobSub: Report it to the office within 15 working days (art. 121)
moveHouseSub: If the address is on your card, exchange the card within 14 days
cardLostSub: Apply for a new one; you get a free temporary certificate
travelSub: With your card and passport: up to 90 days in any 180
familyEndsWithYours: A family permit ends with the permit of the person they joined (art. 162), so you renew together.
pathFileDetail: Sign and send in MOS, then add the UPO receipt
pathWaitingDetail: You may stay and work while the case runs. Dossierly reads every letter the day it arrives.
pathLetterDetail: If the office asks for documents, the deadline appears here
pathLetterOpen: A letter is waiting for your answer
pathVisitDetail: At least 7 days' notice. Bring your passport.
pathAfterDetail: One visit to collect the card
setupBody: Five short questions: your situation, permit, region, card end date and family. Dossierly then shows your file-by date and what to do next.
whatYouCanDo: What you can do while waiting
homeCollect: Collect your card and keep the receipt.
homeRecord: Has the decision arrived? Record it to see what comes next.
